paper_title: CodeRAG: Supportive Code Retrieval on Bigraph for Real-World Code Generation

experiments.research_goal: To determine the contribution of each component in CodeRAG to the overall performance in real-world code generation.

methods.name: Code Anchor
methods.description: A component that serves as a reference point for retrieving supportive codes, enabling adaptive reasoning during code generation.

methods.name: Web Search
methods.description: A component that retrieves external knowledge through web search, enhancing the LLM's ability to generate correct programs.

datasets.name: DevEval
datasets.description: A representative repo-level code generation dataset that aligns with real-world repositories in multiple dimensions, including code distributions and dependency distributions.

key_results: The code anchor component significantly improves retrieval accuracy, as Pass@1 increases by 6.31 points.
The web search component contributes 0.29 Pass@1 improvement, demonstrating its utility in providing external knowledge.
experiments.conclusion: It maps these requirement nodes into code nodes on DS-code graph, where these code nodes are treated as anchors. CODERAG then introduce an agentic process, allowing LLMs to comprehensively retrieve supportive codes through reasoning from these anchors on DS-code graph. Experiments show that CODERAG achieves a significant improvement compared to advanced RAG methods and commercial programming products, highlighting its potential in real-world coding challenges.
evidence: WebSearch) results in 0.29 Pass@1 decreasing (from 58.14 to 57.85), demonstrating that the websearch tool can bring useful information to LLMs.
GraphReason) lead to a significant degradation in performance, with Pass@1 decreasing by 6.31 points (from 58.14 to 51.83).
How do different components in CODERAG contribute to performance improvement?

research_problem_description: Real-world code generation involves retrieving supportive codes for generating correct programs, which is challenging due to complex dependencies and domain knowledge. The paper addresses the need for a retrieval-augmented code generation framework to handle these complexities.
